decisions.reason: Location-based margin analysis builds closely on the firm’s existing energy market data and precise-calculation capabilities, so related knowledge supports interpreting early results and improving the product.
Gas tariff comparison directly builds on the firm’s established gas tariff data and market-communication expertise, giving high absorptive capacity to learn from early results.
Regional electricity tariff calculator uses the firm’s core electricity tariff and billing knowledge, so the firm can readily assimilate feedback and enhance it.

Although related, the regional energy tariff calculator overlaps with the more established B and C and was only mentioned on the website, indicating limited early learning and lower absorptive capacity for differentiating it.

The area definition tool supports the location-based products and draws on the firm’s data-capture and quality processes, though it requires some new GIS-related knowledge that the firm can still assimilate.

The site-specific energy tariff comparison is a complex product line only mentioned on the website, suggesting the firm has difficulty interpreting site-level model results and applying its tariff knowledge to multiple models.
